parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the source of untrusted data is stdin via scanf on line 9, and that the sink is printf on line 11. The format string on line 11 is a compile‑time constant "Value: %" PRId64 "\n", which expands to a standard 64‑bit integer format specifier (e.g., "%lld"). Passing a 64‑bit integer to printf with the correct specifier does not cause integer overflow or wraparound; the value is converted to a string representation safely. No path exists where the integer value is interpreted as a format string or used in an arithmetic operation that could overflow. Therefore the reported vulnerability is not present.
